title: Understanding Java interfaces
answer: An interface defines a contract that implementing classes agree to satisfy. It separates what a component can do from how a particular implementation does it. Interfaces support polymorphism and loose coupling; modern Java interfaces may also contain default, static, and private methods, while their fields are implicitly public static final constants.
